quest.title: Wishes
quest.description: You did not betray the ambitions that had been entrusted to you — the Vision Hunt Decree has been abolished by the Raiden Shogun. The turbulent waves have calmed for now. Time to go see Yae Miko.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x22000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what did you guys do in the Raiden Shogun's Plane of Euthymia anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the Vision Hunt Decree abolished?

choices.text: It was all thanks to Yae Miko.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, gotcha... Paimon was super worried, y'know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So maybe the reason Yae Miko is looking for us now is 'cause she wants to thank us? Let's go find her.

choices.text: We conveyed the wishes of the people.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: What would you like to know about?

choices.text: About the Shogun puppet...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That puppet was built with technology that has been lost to time. Perhaps she, as a god, is the only one privy to the knowledge of its origins...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Still... there is one other thing on this topic that I suspect you may be curious to know.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Before Ei began modifying her own godly form, she took it upon herself to create a prototype puppet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... you mean there are three Raiden Shoguns!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: No, the prototype was merely a proof of concept. Its appearance and intellect were not based on Ei. It was a test.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The original plan was for Ei to simply discard it. But perhaps Ei thought this to be too cruel, because in the end she chose only to seal the power within it.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Later, this puppet wandered Inazuma as an ordinary human male with his own consciousness, until... the Fatui took an interest in him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, not the Fatui!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Some eccentric geniuses in the ranks of the Fatui made adjustments to the prototype, not only unsealing his power, but very likely rendering him even more formidable than his original specifications.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Surely you don't mean...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Mm-hmm. The object of divine creation is the one who has now taken possession of the Gnosis... and the prototype puppet is now known as "The Balladeer."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the... What a crazy story!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It is, isn't it? Who can say whether it's coincidence or destiny.

choices.text: About the Shogun puppet...
About the former Raiden Shogun...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm surprised an outlander like you is aware that there was once a change of Electro Archon... Few citizens of Inazuma are aware of this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Morax told us. He said that the Electro Archon, Baal, has passed away...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. The truth of the matter is that there were two twin gods, Baal and Beelzebul.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Twin gods?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: They won the Archon War together, and when Baal established the Shogunate, Beelzebul became her Kagemusha, or "shadow warrior." In other words, she acted as Baal's body double.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Beelzebul is Ei, with whom we are now both acquainted. Baal's name was "Makoto."

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As far as the world was aware, there were not two, but one. They complemented each other, and they ruled Inazuma jointly. So there was no need for the public to know the truth.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In fact, the name "Baal" and the title of Raiden Shogun was understood to refer to both of them, right up until—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Until what?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Makoto died several hundred years ago in a war that I was not personally involved in. Since then, Ei has assumed the Shogunate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Losing her sister must have been super hard on Ei...

choices.text: Several hundred years ago...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That was when Ei began to change. Makoto was her greatest loss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels like she understands Ei a lot better now after finding that out... So, what kind of god was Makoto?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I didn't spend a great deal of time with her, but my impression was... she was a gentle god, who in each moment cherished the beauty of what was before her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow...

choices.text: About the Shogun puppet...
About the former Raiden Shogun...
#About my {F#brother}{M#sister}...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Sorry, I haven't a clue. I am also unfamiliar with the god you describe.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But if you still have doubts about Ei, I would say they are misplaced.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Not only does she not fit your description, but she voluntarily gave up her Gnosis long ago, severing her ties with Celestia in the process.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Having met her, I don't believe she was the one.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That's good to hear. Otherwise, given that I am her familiar, it could have made our relationship rather awkward, don't you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we aren't looking to pick a fight with you!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehehe... I wish you the best of luck. May you soon discover the truth behind it all.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: #As for your {M#sister}{F#brother}'s whereabouts, I will use all the resources at my disposal to investigate it, and I will also borrow some of Ayato's people from the Shuumatsuban.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'll let you know if I find out anything. Consider it part of my means of thanking you.

choices.text: About the Shogun puppet...
About the former Raiden Shogun...
#About my {F#brother}{M#sister}...
About the next stop on my journey...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: After leaving Inazuma, hmm... I think it would be easiest for you to go to Sumeru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, ooh, Sumeru! We've run into loads of scholars from there on our journey so far.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes, well, Sumeru is the land of the God of Wisdom, where the quest for wisdom and knowledge is never-ending.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But their obsession gives rise to some truly inexplicable things. For example...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In Sumeru, knowledge is holistically managed as a resource.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Knowledge... is a resource?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. I don't know whether it was the sages or Lesser Lord Kusanali who came up with the idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali? That's a cute name.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, you haven't heard? "Lesser Lord Kusanali" is the deity in whom the people of Sumeru place their faith. It's their chosen term of endearment for her.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm sure you must have some things to discuss with her, too. I wish you all the best.

choices.text: About the Shogun puppet...
About the former Raiden Shogun...
#About my {F#brother}{M#sister}...
About the next stop on my journey...
I have no more questions.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Are you sure? Okay then. Oh, Traveler, do you still have the omamori I gave you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course. I'll keep it in a safe place.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Keep it safe? Is that all you intend to do with it?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: There was me thinking that you might hang it around your neck to show off to the world, telling everyone who inquired that it was given to you by none other than Yae Miko, the wise and beautiful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who in their right mind would do that!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehehe... Okay, I'll stop. Now, a question for you. Traveler, what is your ambition?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #To be reunited with my {F#brother}{M#sister}, I guess?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I see... But that is merely a small goal, based on what preoccupies you here and now.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Your ambition should be something that transcends the world below and the starry sky above. Something that shines in unison with fate itself.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Perhaps the reason you do not possess a Vision is that such an ambition has yet to be engendered within you... It's a possibility.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Continue on your journey and maybe that moment will come to pass.

choices.text: I have no more questions.
About the next stop on my journey...
I have no more questions.
Khaenri'ah...
#About my {F#brother}{M#sister}...
About the next stop on my journey...
I have no more questions.
About the former Raiden Shogun...
#About my {F#brother}{M#sister}...
About the next stop on my journey...
I have no more questions.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Why hello... if it isn't the triumphant Traveler. And why might you be visiting the Shrine? A sign of piety, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You literally told us to come meet you here!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Haha... I was just joking. I've been waiting for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like someone's in a pretty good mood.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Catching up with an old friend I hadn't seen in years was truly delightful.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: By the way... I heard that you had a duel before the throne, with a Fatui Harbinger no less. Courageous and astute — I must say, I am most impressed.

choices.text: It was a spur-of-the-moment thing.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Defeating Signora head-on in a duel means that your strength exceeds my expectations.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Still, you did end up victorious. I gather congratulations are in order.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, it sure feels good to finally thwart a Fatui plan for once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They caused plenty of trouble along the way, but at the very least, they didn't get their hands on another Gnosis!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Wait a second... did you say "Gnosis"?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As in, the little thing that looks something like a chess piece?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that's the one! You've seen one, too? Gnoses belong to The Seven — they're what keep them connected to Celestia!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I handed that over.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You did what now?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well... how else was I supposed to save your skin from The Balladeer, exactly?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The Balladeer is No. 6 of the Fatui Harbingers. In terms of strength, he is superior to Signora.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm not the kind of person who risks life and limb for any old reason.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *stammers* For once, Paimon just does not know what to say.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But why was the Gnosis in your hands?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: After Ei created her puppet vessel, she no longer had anywhere to put it.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As her erstwhile closest friend... Ei handed it over to me, and I've kept it in the Grand Narukami Shrine ever since.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: She no longer needs the power of the Gnosis, and in any case, she tells me she has severed ties with Celestia.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Thus, the Gnosis became not only useless, but also a potential source of conflict.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Is that not a good bargain, exchanging it for the one at the core of the plan?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Judging by the results, at least, I daresay I struck a good deal. Hehehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you put it like that, Paimon has to agree... The Traveler is worth more than a Gnosis...

choices.text: No wonder we haven't seen The Balladeer since.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Well, what's done is done, and Paimon hardly thinks we'll be getting it back now. Let's leave the past in the past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, so anyway, you still haven't told us why you called us here today.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehehe. It's to thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You intend to travel all over Teyvat, and the time has come for the Inazuma leg of your trip to come to an end, has it not?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As a mark of my gratitude, I will answer any questions you may have about the road ahead or the events of the past.

choices.text: Never knew I could fetch such a high price.
The Gnosis is long gone, then.
I don't know what came over me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Twenty years ago, the Akademiya had just received Sachin's estate. To celebrate the huge investment, the Akademiya Extravaganza that year was grander than usual.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I was very young then, and I remember seeing posters for the Interdarshan Championship all over the city. I couldn't help but mention it to my father. I even told him that I really liked the look of the diadem — it was so unique.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So he said, "Why don't I win it, so I can let you play with it for a few days?"

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That made me very happy, and I nodded enthusiastically. But to my surprise, he didn't win, and when he got back home, he seemed extremely depressed.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Later, he left home, saying that he wanted to do some investigating in the desert... The quicksand got him not long after that...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...For many years, I couldn't face up to it at all. If I'd just kept my mouth shut, maybe none of it would have ever happened.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your father may have seen Sachin that year.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... So the person we came across in our investigation, who went into the desert twenty years ago... it was...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Haha... Is that why Sachin thought I looked familiar? I can't believe it...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...My father was always too kind for his own good. Sachin's research would have saddened him greatly — he must have gone into the desert when he heard about it to find those who were still suffering... It all makes sense now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I've tried telling myself so many times over the years that maybe his sudden depression wasn't because he didn't win the competition, maybe something else was going on that I wasn't aware of... But in the end, it all started with me mentioning the competition to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, Kaveh...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I... I destroyed the diadem. There will never be another tragedy like this again. Never again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Don't mention the results of the investigation.)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Sorry... My mind was still on the Championship. Look at me, rambling away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You look really upset... Are you sure you're okay?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm fine. What's past is past — we need to look towards the future.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Where were you while the rest of us were eating together?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I don't recall being obligated to report my whereabouts to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Did you go find another hidey-hole to read in? You need to change your ways, you know. You can't survive on books alone.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Surviving on meals paid for by you would be harder still.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmph, whatever, it doesn't take a genius to guess what you've been up to... You were investigating Sachin, weren't you? It was obvious from your notes. However, I don't believe his research alone would've been enough to pique your interest.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: His way of doing things is disturbing, while you... Well, to be fair, your philosophy disgusts me too, but you and Sachin are nothing alike. I don't imagine your views intersect at all. Egoism and nihilism are not the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: My personal interest aside, Sachin's legacy is not entirely meaningless — he conducted experiments on a great scale, and left his findings behind.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Also, thanks for the compliment. But I'm actually just passing through — I didn't come here for the conversation. Well, not this one at least.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What do you mean? What topic of conversation could be more sacred among scholars than the exploration of differing philosophies?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, based on what I've learned, Sachin and his "disturbing way of doing things" — as you put it — is very likely to have met your father twenty years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...What did you say?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Wait, so... No, surely that doesn't mean...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hah. So that's why he thought I looked familiar. My father must've gone into the desert due to his influence...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm afraid so.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Good thing I shattered that diadem. From now on... nothing like that will ever have to happen again.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The boundaries of knowledge are ever-expanding. Someone else will inevitably pick up the same line of research one day, and Vahumana regards it as a reasonable research direction.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, not this again... Even if you're right, and people are bound to fall into the same intellectual traps, things won't necessarily go the same way again next time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You have to admit that the actions of one individual don't always predict the behavior of the group, and vice-versa. Take Sachin, for instance. He's quite an anomaly.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And so is the one who stopped him — you. Conflicts of this nature are indeed exceptional, but it will occur again in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You said it yourself — the actions of one individual cannot predict the behavior of a whole group. You know that not everyone would have chosen as you did.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Even so, I stand by my views. You can forget about trying to convince me.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's fine. We've been arguing over this for years, and I don't hold any hope of you understanding. The issue we're debating has long since moved on from who's right and who's wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Thanks for letting me know all this.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I said, thanks for letting me know. Hey! Stop acting like you didn't hear me! You're doing this on purpose, aren't you!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: They say that earnest thanks should be given thrice, so... One more time, please.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, how did it go? I assume that Lord Sangemah Bay's assistance helped you discover something, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Sachin was not a good person, and there's definitely something wrong with that Diadem of Knowledge!

choices.text: Indeed.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Then in that case, shouldn't you be doing something about it?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: For instance, telling the Akademiya that they should give up the Diadem—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We already told the Akademiya, but...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: But what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kaveh smashed the diadem.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Whaaaaat!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Calm down, Dori! Why are you getting so worked up?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: My diadem... My beautiful diadem...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Ah, this was supposed to be the perfect plan! I feed you the information, you discover the issue with the diadem, and then I just wait until the Akademiya sells it off at a low price...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: And now it was all for nothing! Grr, curse that Kaveh! The interest rate on the Mora he owes me is about to get much higher!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh, so that's why you told us about this. Yeah, Paimon did think you were being unusually generous...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: My diadem! Ugh, I'm furious! That's it, no extension on his payment this month, no matter what reason he gives!

choices.text: We also discovered that.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: Hello, I am the Vizier. Do you need any help?

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: If you wished to see the Interdarshan Championship, then unfortunately, the portion taking part in Sumeru City has concluded.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: ...Hold on, on closer inspection you seem to be that guest commentator.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: My apologies. I thank you for the contributions you made to the Akademiya Extravaganza. It's all thanks to your help that the first round concluded so smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: But I might have been overindulgent in my praise. I heard the Interdarshan Championship has also encountered similar difficulties before... This time, both the contestants and viewers have been spared any harm. How fortunate.

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: Greetings. You may call me "Master Treasure Appraiser, Prospective Antiques Collector, and Future Prominent Businessman Feresht."

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: Have you heard? The Akademiya is hosting some kind of celebration along with a competition. Supposedly, the champion's prize is an extremely rare treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: I think it was called... the diadem of... something. Ah. It doesn't matter. The first trick to being an expert appraiser of treasures is to avoid getting intimidated by a treasure's name!

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: In terms of appraising antique collections, I'm only slightly less refined than my father. If you want to know how much a certain treasure is worth, just bring it to me and I'll let you know after a glance.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: It's not often that the Akademiya hosts an event like this. We need to increase the number of patrols inside the city for this special occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: This isn't even especially for the competition. In fact, it is the increase in tourists that require us to take additional care.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: There are no shortage of devious people who are willing to take advantage of these festivities to mask their own nefarious deeds.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: ...Should you deny that the Championship rates Darshans based on their scores, please recall that we all entered our respective Darshans via our test scores.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: To overlook the scores is to overlook the very basis for all assessments made by the Darshans.

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: In turn, you should remember before you overemphasize the scores, that they are only representative of how each contestant performs for specific tasks exclusive to the competition.

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: Moreover, we also need to consider other probabilistic factors such as weather, geography, morale and so on.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: Oh? And we didn't need to consider this when we were testing into our Darshans?

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: A sophistic comparison! My test scores can represent my capabilities, but it does not showcase the totality of what a Darshan represents.

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: A foolish opinion as usual. No offense intended.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: Disagree though you may, scores determine the rankings and results speak for everything.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: Even if we find a calm place to think, we will inevitably be interrupted by noisy students.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: To be honest, I was never interested in these celebratory events or competitions when I was in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: Winning the Championship doesn't really help add any credit to your research, and any renown gained from it only amounts to some short-lived attention.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: ...Realistically speaking, there are few people as practical as I am.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Star... star course deviations...

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Ah, if I continue my studies down this path, I might just be able to see why there is a separation between my theories and the calculations.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: The Interdarshan Championships have done a lot of good this time. If Rtawahist hadn't selected Miss Layla as the representative, I would have never consulted her research.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: I can only say that Miss Layla keeps too low a profile. Such incredible research needs to be seen by more people.

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: A pity that knowledge so great is constrained by matters of Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: And when there are wealthy sponsors, the wealth is not fed into valuable research but rather burned on frivolous competitions...

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: You mean the sponsor? Hm... I haven't heard much about them, but they should be a good person.

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: Even merchants who think of nothing but profit should not be judged with prejudice so long as they are willing to place emphasis on the development and preservation of knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: ...Because, when it comes down to it, almost anything is better than someone who wastes money.

dialogues.speaker: Makhfi
